agent_notes: Every 'Likhmisar' record independently found (GeoNames, census mirrors, mapsofindia, jatland) points to the same real place: a pair of villages 'Likhmisar Utrada' (लिखमीसर उतरादा) and 'Likhmisar Dikhnada' (लिखमीसर दिखनादा), both in Sridungargarh tehsil of Bikaner district -- NOT Lunkaransar tehsil / Mahajan sub-tehsil where the 34-gaon firing range villages sit. No source placed a 'Likhmisar' inside Lunkaransar tehsil. Two detailed Rajasthan Patrika features specifically about the Mahajan Field Firing Range's 1984-85 acquisition of 34 villages (searched in full) name roughly a dozen displaced villages between them (Bhojrasar, Kumhana, Motlai, Khanisar, Thoia, Manera, Duder, Khajuwala, Dantur, Pugal, Mohangarh, Nachna) and never mention Likhmisar. A full-text check of the archive.org Rajasthan District Gazetteer (Bikaner) also returned no match. Spellings that matter: 'Likhmisar Utrada'/'Likhmisar Uttarada' (उत्तरादा) vs 'Likhmisar Dikhnada'/'Dikhnada' (दिखणादा) are the two real administrative units; plain 'Likhmisar' (GeoNames id 1264927) appears to be an aggregator's collapse of these two. Facebook hits (a temple jagran video, an ashram page) use the bare name 'Likhmisar' and most likely refer to the Sridungargarh villages, not a Mahajan-range village, though this could not be confirmed with certainty. Given this, direct_mention is set to false on every source below pending human verification of whether the community list's 'Likhmisar' entry (positions 33-34, originally blank/reconstructed) is a genuine distinct 34th village or a misidentification of the Sridungargarh place.
